items.title: Harbour cranes go quiet as the night shift ends
items.author: R. de Vries
items.excerpt: The last container came off the deck just after five. What follows is the hour nobody photographs, when the terminal belongs to the gulls.

items.title: A small library of forgotten map projections
items.author: S. Okonkwo
items.excerpt: Between Mercator and Peters sit two hundred attempts nobody adopted. Some of them are beautiful, and one of them is nearly correct.

items.title: Why your RSS reader shows the wrong date
items.author: M. Alvarez
items.excerpt: RFC 822, RFC 3339, and a decade of publishers splitting the difference. A short field guide to timestamps that lie.

items.title: The last independent print shop on the canal
items.author: J. Bakker
items.excerpt: Four presses, one apprentice, and a lease that runs out in March. The owner is not worried, which is itself worth reporting.

items.title: Field recordings from a decommissioned lighthouse
items.author: T. Lindqvist
items.excerpt: Thirty hours of wind, one unexplained bell, and a foghorn that has not been connected to anything since 1998.

items.title: Reading the weather from a hundred year old ledger
items.author: P. Nowak
items.excerpt: A grain merchant's daily notes turn out to be the most complete rainfall record in the province, kept entirely by accident.
